title: QA wave R1: checklist run `priority:P0` (16 items) at e4e5c6e3
body:
Part of #9296.
Blocked-by: #9298

Release-gating smoke. Runs first among the execution rounds because a red P0 changes what the rest of the wave is worth doing.

## Contract

- Resolve the set deterministically — **never pick items by eye**: `node scripts/checklist-select.mjs priority:P0 --json`. Expect 16 active items (5 `browser`, so the R0 console build is a hard prerequisite; 8 carry an `automated.ref`).
- Execute via the **`checklist-test` skill**, obeying `docs/qa/platform-checklist/RUNNER.md` and the `dogfood-verification` skill. Those are the protocol; this card does not restate them.
- Run in the QA tree R0 provisioned. Own port + own `file:/tmp/qa-wave/<item>.db` per concurrently running item; 2–3 browser items in parallel at most.
- Runner subagents must be dispatched on **opus**, each handed: that item's JSON, RUNNER.md, the dogfood skill, its own port/DB, and the results-never-land-in-the-repo rule.
- Pin the `revision` the selector reports into the run record — a verdict is only valid for the revision it ran against.
- RUNNER rule 7 applies with full force here: **every P0 `fail` gets re-derived by a second, independent agent from the captured evidence alone** before it is written down.

## Output

One `qa-run` issue (`bug` too if any clause fails, `regression` when a P0/P1 breaks something that used to work): env fingerprint · scope + per-item revisions · per-clause verdict table with **text** oracle evidence · a reproduction rule per `fail` · derived item verdicts + fixture gaps. Text only, no screenshots. Link it back here and on #9296.
